title: KV sparse compartmentalization and proactive migration playbook
creator: Priya Nambiar
description:
Problem: We observe persistent long-tail GPU memory fragmentation in the KV cache under mixed workloads (chat + streaming + long-context inference). Fragmentation increases effective memory pressure, forces higher-quantization fallbacks, and raises per-token cost. This ticket defines a pragmatic allocator and migration playbook to reduce fragmentation, improve cache hit stability, and cooperate with continuous batching heuristics.

Goal: Introduce a compartmentalized KV allocation model with lightweight migration hints and background compaction that respects latency SLOs. Reduce measurable fragmentation (wasted free bytes in GPU pool) by >= 35% on mixed chat workloads while keeping 99th percentile generation latency regression <= 3%.

High-level approach: 1) Partition the KV pool into logical compartments (hot, warm, cold, transient) with tunable size ratios per-model. 2) Allocate new KV entries into compartments chosen by a fast heuristic (sequence-length bucket + recent hit rate + request type). 3) Emit migration hints for entries that cross heat thresholds rather than immediate relocations. 4) Run background epochal compaction that coalesces small free fragments into contiguous chunks during low-util windows; limit compaction CPU/GPU overhead via rate limiting and backpressure from the serving runtime. 5) Integrate allocator signals into continuous batching router so that batch packing favors entries colocated in same compartment to maximize KV locality. 6) Expose telemetry and gating flags for gradual rollout.
acceptance_criteria: Fragmentation metric (free-frag %) reduced by >= 35% on representative mixed workload replay compared to baseline
No more than 3% regression in 99th percentile generation latency under production traffic in canary
KV hit rate (post-eviction) improves or remains equal for top-10 models in our benchmark suite
Feature gated and can be disabled without restart; rollout plan documented and tested
Telemetry dashboards show per-model compartment occupancy, migration rates, compaction throughput
implementation_notes: Allocator components: fast placement path in C++ runtime for alloc/free; lightweight metadata per entry (compartment id, age counter, last-access epoch) limited to 16 bytes to avoid overhead
Compartment sizing: start with defaults hot:10%, warm:50%, cold:30%, transient:10% and enable per-model overrides via model-config in catalog
Migration hints: mark entries as MOVABLE with score = f(age, hits, access_interval); background thread performs batch migrations to minimize kernel launch overhead

Compaction strategy: epochal sweep that coalesces adjacent free ranges into superblocks; use GPU-aware page coalescing where supported, otherwise fallback to device-host-device copy with concurrency limits
Continuous batching integration: router exposes batch-local placement hint for requests; batching logic will group requests targeting same compartment to reduce KV scattering
Safety: migrations are performed non-blocking using double-buffered pointers and atomic swap; fallbacks for failure include rollback and marking entry as pinned for X minutes
Config knobs: migration_rate_per_gpu, compaction_window_seconds, compartment_ratios, min_migration_batch_size, pin_ttl_seconds
plan: Spike: implement in-memory simulator to validate heuristics with historical traffic (2w)
Prototype: runtime-only implementation behind feature flag; unit tests + microbenchmarks (3w)
Telemetry: add heatmap, fragmentation gauges, migration counters to Console (1w)
Canary: deploy on low-traffic region for 1 week, compare to baseline via A/B test (2w)
Rollout: widen to dedicated clusters + release notes + migration safety audit (2w)
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: aggressive migration may increase tail latency. Mitigation: rate-limit migrations and prioritize off-peak windows; add latency budget check before compaction steps.
Risk: incorrect compartment sizing for some models. Mitigation: expose per-model overrides and autosize suggestion job that analyzes historical heat metrics.
Risk: extra metadata increases memory overhead. Mitigation: compress metadata into 16 bytes and measure overhead; revert if net memory wins disappear.
Risk: interactions with quantized model variants causing incompatible KV layouts. Mitigation: maintain separate pools per-quantization-profile and provide safe fallback routing.
tests: Unit: allocator fast-path allocation/free, metadata consistency, atomic migration swap
Integration: run mixed-workload replay (chat+completion+embedding-only) and collect fragmentation, latency, and hitrate
Stress: overloaded scenario with continuous long contexts to exercise compaction backpressure
Chaos: kill background migrator mid-epoch and verify safe rollback and no memory leaks
telemetry_and_alerting: Derived: free_frag_ratio = 1 - (max_contiguous_free / total_free), alert if > 0.5 for > 5m
Dashboards: per-model timeline with compartment occupancy, batch-locality score, and fragmentation heatmap
rollout_notes: Start canary with migration_rate_per_gpu = 0.05 and compaction_window_seconds = 900
Observe migration_failures < 0.1% and 99p latency regression < 3% before widening
If regressions observed, decrease migration_rate_per_gpu or disable compaction during peak hours
